newsitem.title: NORWAY: Kvaerner heads race for Danish Siri deal.
newsitem.headline: Kvaerner heads race for Danish Siri deal.

text.p: Norwegian engineering and construction group Kvaerner ASA is tipped as favourite to win the contract for development of the Siri oilfield in the Danish sector of the North Sea, a company source said on Friday.

The value of the contract depends on the development solution chosen by the operator, state Norwegian oil company Den norske stats oljeselskap AS, but industry analysts estimated the deal would be worth between 1.2 and 1.8 billion crowns.
"I have heard rumors today that we will win the contract," the source in Kvaerner told Reuters.

Kvaerner announced on Friday that Statoil had awarded it a $1 billion contract to build the world's largest floating gas production platform for the Aasgard development off mid-Norway in the Norwegian Sea.
Originally Kvaerner was shortlisted for the Siri project with Norwegian rival offshore group Aker Maritime ASA, but a spokesman for Aker said the company was out of the race.
"As it appears now, we are not engaged in Siri. But if Statoil choses another (development) solution we could come back into the picture," Aker spokesman Torbjoern Andersen said.
Market rumors indicated that Statoil has opted for a jack up rig for Siri, which was discovered in 1995.
Statoil was expected to announce the contract in early February, but sources said the decision had been delayed to sometime later in the month.
"We are in the closing phase," said Kjell Ravndal, project leader for Siri in Statoil Denmark.
